bottom_line: In COPERNICUS, carvedilol vs placebo reduced the combined risk of death or hospitalization for a cardiovascular reason by 27% (95% CI, 16% to 37%).
implications: In this trial of 2289 euvolemic patients with severe chronic heart failure (ejection fraction ⬍25%), carvedilol (vs placebo) was associated with lower Kaplan-Meier 1-year cumulative risk of death or hospitalization for a cardiovascular reason (41.6% vs 30.2%) and a reported 27% lower risk (95% CI, 16% to 37%). The document also reports fewer serious adverse events with carvedilol (39.0% vs 45.5%). These findings pertain to the enrolled population (eg, 'but not volume-overloaded') and do not by themselves establish effects in patients who were not enrolled.

major_points.text: Randomized, double-blind assignment of euvolemic severe HF patients (EF <25%) to placebo vs carvedilol with average follow-up 10.4 months.
major_points.quote: We randomly assigned 2289 patients with symptoms of heart failure at rest or on minimal exertion and with an ejection fraction ⬍25% (but not volume-overloaded) to double-blind treatment with either placebo (n⫽1133) or carvedilol (n⫽1156) for an average of 10.4 months.

major_points.text: Carvedilol reduced death or cardiovascular hospitalization: Kaplan-Meier 1-year cumulative risks 41.6% vs 30.2% and 27% relative risk reduction with 95% CI 16% to 37%.
major_points.quote: Kaplan-Meier 1-year cumulative risks of 41.6% and 30.2%, respectively. These differences reflected a 27% lower risk as a result of treatment with carvedilol (95% CI, 16% to 37%), P⫽0.00002

absolute_effects.text: Kaplan-Meier 1-year cumulative risks of death or hospitalization for a cardiovascular reason: 41.6% placebo vs 30.2% carvedilol.
absolute_effects.quote: corresponding to Kaplan-Meier 1-year cumulative risks of 41.6% and 30.2%, respectively.

absolute_effects.text: Kaplan-Meier 1-year cumulative risks of death or hospitalization for heart failure: 37.9% placebo vs 25.5% carvedilol.
absolute_effects.quote: corresponding to Kaplan- Meier 1-year cumulative risks of 37.9% and 25.5%, respec- tively.

absolute_effects.text: Hospitalized for any reason: 432 (38.1%) placebo vs 372 (32.2%) carvedilol.

harms.text: Serious adverse event of heart failure: 273 (24.1%) placebo vs 192 (16.6%) carvedilol (P<0.0001).
